v.why: Removing the direct input-output edge when node 2's output edge is absent risks disconnecting the cell, collapsing accuracy.
With edge 1 absent, node 2 depends solely on node 1, so cutting edge 0 kills both intermediate nodes.
Replacing none adds an entire new computational path to the output, a much bigger gain than swapping one existing op.
Restoring the residual shortcut greatly aids trainability of the stacked network compared with swapping other ops.
Replacing parameter-free pooling with a 3x3 conv yields a larger gain than replacing other ops, including the conv itself.
Swapping the most useful op for pooling loses more capacity than swapping weaker ops.
Removing the identity residual path hurts deep stacked cells more than removing other ops on that edge.
Without the direct edge, edge 5 carries much of the output signal, so cutting it is more damaging.
When edge 1 is absent, edge 2 is node 2's only input, so a skip keeps node 2 alive and its downstream paths useful.
Removing edge 4 without the direct shortcut leaves fewer paths to the output and raises the risk of disconnection.

raw:
These hypotheses are based on known structural features of NAS-Bench-201, mainly connectivity and the residual path. I have not checked them against the benchmark tables.

1. Removing the input→output edge (edge 3) hurts more when edge 5 is already none, because the cell is more likely to become disconnected.
2. Removing edge 0 hurts more when edge 1 is none, because node 2 then depends only on node 1.
3. Setting edge 5 to nor_conv_3x3 gains more when it replaces none, because that adds a whole new path through node 2.
4. Setting edge 3 to skip_connect gains more when it replaces none, because that restores the residual shortcut.
5. Setting edge 1 to nor_conv_3x3 gains more when it replaces avg_pool_3x3, the weakest op that keeps the edge.
6. Setting edge 4 to avg_pool_3x3 is worse when it replaces nor_conv_3x3.
7. Removing edge 3 is worse when edge 3 is skip_connect, because deep stacks lose their identity path.
8. Removing edge 5 is worse when edge 3 is none, because edge 5 then carries a large share of the output.
9. Setting edge 2 to skip_connect gains more when edge 1 is none, because it is node 2's only remaining input.
10. Removing edge 4 is worse when edge 3 is none, because fewer paths reach the output.
